clue.text: Contract that's set up between banks?

definitions.meaning: to contract a text is to shorten or condense it
read as two words, a structure built to span a river from one bank to the other

explanation.surface: A puzzle over some financial agreement drawn up between two banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'banks' of the surface are lenders; the second reading wants river banks, and the answer split as A BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a book or speech is to cut it down, which is what contracting it does.

clue.text: Reckon court must put one inside as fanatic

parts.note: to reckon is to add up or count
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A judge decides the court must lock up a zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is a devotee or obsessive enthusiast, the sense of an addict of a hobby.

clue.text: Admit set is incomplete

indicators.note: is incomplete tells us the word for set loses its final letter

parts.note: a set is a radio or television receiver

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that their collection lacks a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is incomplete' cuts the last R from RECEIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit guests is to let them in, to welcome or take them in.

clue.text: Restrict the flow of people's expression of anger

parts.note: to dam a river is to hold back its water
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Holding back a crowd provokes an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation! is an oath, a curse spoken in fury.

clue.text: One presenting picture so awful about rise of EC?

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters surround the turned-round pair
so awful says the letters of the preceding words are badly put together and must be rearranged
rise of, in a down clue, tells us the letters EC are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: EC is the European Community, taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic of Europe paints a dreadful picture of the EC's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so awful' gives EUROSPTIC from its fodder, and 'rise of' turns the pair upwards before 'about' wraps round it. 'presenting' is a link; 'One' is a person who fits the whole description.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurosceptic is a person hostile to the European Union, and the clue's 'One' stands for such a person.

clue.text: One river or another — to another returned

parts.note: the Po is a river in Italy
taken as written

indicators.note: returned says the word for the second river is read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A geography muddle naming one river after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or another' is the definition: yet another river. 'returned' turns CAM into MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the river flowing past Washington DC, so it is a further example of a waterway.

clue.text: Quarter of a pint in beer container

indicators.note: quarter of a four-letter word is its first single letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small measure of ale sits in the cask.
explanation.walkthrough: PINT has four letters, so its quarter is P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons of ale.

clue.text: Keep out of ghetto, we recommend

indicators.note: out of says the answer is taken from within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to stay away from a poor district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep out' reads as a phrase, but 'Keep' alone is the definition, a castle's stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest, central fortified part of a castle.

clue.text: As if I'm distressed about old criminals!

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the letter for old
distressed means upset or disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone protests in mock horror at being taken for an old gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' turns ASIFIM into MAFISI, and 'about' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafiosi are members of the Mafia, the Sicilian organised crime gangs.

clue.text: Conceals the end

definitions.meaning: screens or veils from view, as a drape does a window
informal for death or disaster, as in 'it's all over for him'

explanation.definitionFit: Curtains hide a window, and 'curtains for you' means finality or death.

clue.text: Stories of Italian love or of French romance, possibly

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the preceding word might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Tales of Italian love or of French romance, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ROMANCE to CAMERON. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a fourteenth-century collection of a hundred Italian tales, many of love.

clue.text: Disc made of iron used in combat

indicators.note: used in says the symbol for iron goes inside the word for combat

parts.note: combat means fighting, war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A metal disc forged for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a thin round piece, such as the communion host or a silicon slice.

clue.text: Friend in fur not getting chill

indicators.note: not getting says these letters are removed from the word for fur

parts.note: chinchilla is a soft grey fur from the rodent of that name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pal in a fur coat stays warm.
explanation.walkthrough: In rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is British slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'china plate', rhyming with mate, so the word means a pal.

clue.text: Outstanding return for county's brilliant star

parts.note: super means excellent, outstanding

indicators.note: return for says the county's name is read backwards

parts.note: Avon was an English county around Bristol

explanation.surface: A county gets an excellent result thanks to its star player.
explanation.walkthrough: The county was an English one around Bristol from 1974 to 1996; 'return for' reads it backwards, giving a word for a new star.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and briefly blazes far brighter than normal.

clue.text: Little money clear person comes up with in this

definitions.text: Little money clear person comes up with in this

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny, a small coin
overt means open and plain to see

indicators.note: comes up, in a down clue, says the word for person is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a party is a person, especially in law

explanation.surface: Someone earns so little that whatever they clear keeps them stuck in want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns PARTY to YTRAP. The whole clue also describes the trap: earning more yields little extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A poverty trap is where earning more loses benefits, so a worker stays poor.

clue.text: Book that's good, but not first edition?

definitions.text: Book that's good, but not first edition?

parts.words: Book that's good, but not first edition?
parts.note: the Good Book is the Bible; a later, amended English translation of it is not the original printing

explanation.definitionFit: The Revised Version is an 1880s English Bible translation updating the King James text.

clue.text: Mental confusion, losing head in violent downpour

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden mental disturbance

explanation.surface: Someone gets so muddled in a cloudburst they lose their head.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a brainstorm is a fit of confusion; 'losing head' removes its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is heavy rain falling with force.

clue.text: Was no safety device put up for this cutting tool?

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, says the whole run of words is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a net catches a falling acrobat

explanation.surface: A worried question about a saw's lack of a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses WASNONET as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small fine-toothed carpentry saw for cutting joints.

clue.text: Change for better infernal nuisance causing embarrassment

indicators.note: change for says the letters of the words that follow are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A hellish pest needs to change for the better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change for better' reads as reform, but 'Change for' signals rearranging BETTER INFERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is a person whose unconventional behaviour shocks or embarrasses others.

clue.text: Beautiful road a driver doesn't want to leave

definitions.text: a driver doesn't want to leave

parts.note: fair means lovely or beautiful
a way is a road or route

explanation.surface: A motorist loves a scenic road and won't turn off it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'driver' is a golf club, or golfer, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the fairway is the mown strip where a golfer wants the drive to land.

clue.text: Boat for which portage is less of a problem?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

definitions.text: for which portage is less of a problem
definitions.meaning: portage is carrying a boat overland, easier when it weighs less

explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a cargo barge, and a craft of lower weight is easier to haul.

clue.text: Collected maps on time, in the end

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: Someone finally gathers their maps on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: As a rule, not many are involved in it

definitions.text: As a rule, not many are involved in it

parts.words: As a rule, not many are involved in it
parts.note: 'As a rule' reads as 'usually', but it means in the matter of ruling: a government by a few

explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is a state governed by a small group.

clue.text: A case ended prematurely in these courts

indicators.note: ended prematurely says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a legal case

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is cut short in these halls of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ended prematurely' drops the last L of TRIAL. 'courts' are courtyards, not law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards in Roman houses or large buildings.

clue.text: It makes sense to take aim

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, vision
to ... a gun is to aim it along its ...

explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the senses, and to look along a gun's barrel is to aim it.

clue.text: Could be worse off as a farm worker

indicators.note: off says the word's letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A farmhand may be worse off than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worse off' reads as poorer, but 'off' signals rearranging WORSE. 'Could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sower plants seed, one of the tasks done by a farmhand.

clue.text: Co-partner ruined, on the other hand

indicators.note: ruined says the word is wrecked and its letters must be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A business associate is bankrupt, though on the other hand...
explanation.definitionFit: Per contra is Latin for conversely or by contrast.

clue.text: Flat sheets of paper

definitions.meaning: informal for a home or apartment
a block of writing paper fixed at one edge

explanation.definitionFit: A pad is slang for one's lodging, and also a notebook or writing block.

clue.text: With method arranged, carried out ambush

parts.note: a way is a method
laid means set out or arranged, as a table is laid

explanation.surface: An ambush is staged with a well-planned method.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay someone is to lie in wait and attack them.

clue.text: Dog appears to eat into fish

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog
to fret is to wear away or gnaw

explanation.surface: A dog seems to bite into a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomfret is an edible fish of the Atlantic and Indo-Pacific.
